chapter: Army band, Lena Horne, Billie Holiday and the 1950s
title: Ethel Waters and Fletcher's work for Black Swan
summary: In LA Horace worked a Central Avenue club with Ethel Waters; he notes Fletcher started her out as music director for the Black Swan label with Clara Smith, Bessie Smith and Bert Williams.

story.theme_name: Singers and the musicians who accompanied them
story.community_name: Bessie, Mamie, Ma Rainey: the classic blues queens

blocks.x: I got a job down there working at a club right on Central Avenue, and I'll tell you another lady was on the bill -- Ethel Waters was the star attraction. So this could go on. But these things happened. It sounds like fairy tales, but it really happened.
: Ethel Waters had been around a long time, actually, cause she was very big in the mid-twenties.
My brother, you know, started her out --
: That's right. on the Black Swan label
(Unaudible) for Pace and Handy, music company, on the Black Swan 78 label in New York City.
: Yeah. He was musical director for that label when they first started.

Yes, Fletcher was musical director for that. (Unaudible) And he had such singers as Clara Smith, the blues singer, Bessie Smith, another Henderson, Rosa Henderson. He had the late Bert Williams on there, The comedian, and who else? I was a little stinker then in school, but I used to look forward to come and joinin' him then, but those were great days. And then Fletcher had his own band. This is how he began to start these bands to going. That was a great thing.
